primary_sources.role: defines the deer mouse isoform site sets

primary_sources.cite: Natarajan et al., PLOS Genetics 2015, doi:10.1371/journal.pgen.1005681

published_findings_to_test.finding: Deer mouse alpha-globin isoforms are defined by five sites: 50, 57, 60, 64, 71 (alphaI=PGAGS, alphaII=HGAGS, alphaIII=HAGDG); beta-globin by four sites: 62, 72, 128, 135 (betaI=GGAA, betaII=ASSS).
published_findings_to_test.test: Do epistaeon's detected epistatic sites for HBA/HBB recover these positions above chance?

published_findings_to_test.finding: Beta-chain isoform differences in O2 affinity are attributable to DPG sensitivity, not intrinsic affinity.
published_findings_to_test.test: Does epistaeon assign the beta sites to a coupled group distinct from the alpha sites?

published_findings_to_test.finding: High-altitude deer mice carry alphaI/betaI; the high-affinity electromorph is at high frequency above 2750 m.
published_findings_to_test.test: Directionality check only. Note the white paper asserts the opposite polarity for alpha57/alpha64.

structures.notes: Human, deoxy (T) state. About half the alpha1beta2 contacts differ in the R state. Alpha-beta pairs are contacts at exactly one interface and never both.

known_limitations: BLOCKING: no Peromyscus maniculatus sequence in the HBA1, HBA2 or HBB TOGA2 alignments, though three assemblies exist in TOGA2. The focal species of this study is absent.
BLOCKING: Merganetta armata has no TOGA2 assembly under any reference, so the waterfowl arm cannot be run from TOGA2 input at all.
HBA1 34.5% and HBA2 44.0% of codons are gaps or masked bases; expect weak signal.
No complete 2^K recombinant phenotype panel exists; Storz assayed isoform combinations, not all genotypes.
The white paper's claim that alpha57 and alpha64 sit at the alpha1beta1 interface is contradicted by 2HHB: both are haem-pocket residues, over 15 A from the nearest beta1 residue.
expected_outcome_note: A verdict of not_testable for the species-specific claims is the likely honest result. Do not manufacture a replication by substituting a different rodent.
